test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 12 Feb 2021 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: A severe cyclone that hit Odisha in May 2019 was given the name 'Fani' (pronounced as Foni). What does this name mean?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Snake**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Extremely severe cyclonic Fani hit the Odisha coast in Puri early morning with a wind speed of around 175 kmph.(Hence option 2 correct)
 
• The name of the Cyclone 'Fani', pronounced as 'Foni' was suggested by Bangladesh.
 
 
• ​ It means 'Snake' or 'hood of a snake'.
 
 
 
• The worst one, a super cyclone had hit the state in 1999, killing more than 15,000 people of Odisha.
 
• The India Meteorological Department issued a “yellow warning” for the Odisha coast, predicting heavy to very heavy rainfall at some places ahead of the landfall of Cyclone Fani.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The cyclonic storm 'Nilofer', which originated in the Arabian Sea and affected parts of Gujrat in 2014.
 
• The cyclone Hudhud affected Andhra Pradesh and Odisha coast along the Bay of Bengal in 2014.
 
• Cyclone Titli tore into coastal areas of Orissa and Andhra Pradesh states with winds of up to 150km/h (93mph)
